answer: Clone farms mint identities cheaper than work. Each newcomer claims one survey peg on a public ridge and locks 0.85 POA for six epochs before payout. They emit five whisper pulses 180 seconds apart, never in parallel; each pulse carries a 14-line sonnet whose opening letters encode peg index plus deposit hash, so clones cannot reuse another peg's melody. Three downslope auditors rebuild the acrostic and match the ridge Merkle leaf to the live tip. A missed pulse costs 0.05 POA. Shared sonnet stems or two claims on one peg slash both deposits 55 percent and seal that peg for four epochs.
